playbook.notes: Version 2 (answers candidate) = shipped version 1 (its trigger rules, its eleven cast rules in their order, no attack block: Forge attacks) plus four cast rules for the deck's answers: rules 2-4 (wipes, read before everything but the hold) and rule 11 (the removal enchantments, after the enchantress engine and before the other threats). Written from the 200 games of the league of twelve (league-run #3, seed 20261250), where the seat won 64. Seen in / cast from hand in / in hand on the seat's last own turn of a loss: Extinguish All Hope 68/14/29, Culling Ritual 60/13/28, Cacophony Unleashed 59/9/22, Calix 63/21/31, The Eldest Reborn 57/20/20, Grasp of Fate 54/24/18, Battle at the Helvault 47/17/16, Binding the Old Gods 43/20/13 (Path to Exile 74/76/1, Cast Out 46/43/1 and Doomwake Giant 56/52/6 are cast by Forge already and left to it). The library hold of version 1 was not why they sat: under 25 cards on 6 of 104 held turns at most. Boards counted from the zone events and the deck lists (creature tokens counted as creatures without the enchantment type). Rule 2: Extinguish All Hope, else Cacophony Unleashed (destroy all nonenchantment creatures; most of this deck's creatures are enchantment creatures and survive) when an opponent has five or more creatures and more than we have. On the turns Extinguish sat in hand with six lands in a loss, our creatures were 1/3/6 (quartiles), nonenchantment 0/1/4, the largest opposing board 4/7/11; the condition held in 26 of the 34 losses where the card was castable, a median two own turns before the end, and in 14 of 23 such wins (a one-sided wipe there costs little). Rule 3: the same two when an opponent has eight or more creatures and more power than we have, however wide we are. Rule 4: Culling Ritual (destroys every nonland permanent of mana value 2 or less, both sides, tokens included; adds mana for each) when an opponent has six or more creatures and more than we have: it costs us Sol Ring, Signet, the two-mana enchantresses, so a narrower trigger than the one-sided wipe; it held in 19 to 25 of the 33 castable losses. Rule 11: Grasp of Fate, Binding the Old Gods, The Eldest Reborn, Calix and Battle at the Helvault are permanents whose targets are chosen as their trigger or chapter resolves, so a play rule casts them and Forge still aims them. Forge kept them on 54 to 104 turns of losses with the lands for them; a person casts removal that also draws off the enchantresses and feeds Anikthea's copies. Placed after the engine so the enchantresses come first. Not expressible: what a wipe destroys of ours (the creatures metric counts the enchantment creatures that survive), opponents' cheap permanents for Culling Ritual, and which permanent Grasp, Binding, Helvault, Calix's -3, Cast Out and Path aim at (Forge's choice).  Shipped as version 2 on 2026-11-14 from ab-run #31: on the same 200 tables of bots (seed 20261300, opponents drawn from the other eleven bots under their playbooks of 2026-11-13) it won 63 against version 1's 52 (+5.5 points, 95% -1 to +12, exact test 0.16); the cards the new rules name were cast in 415 of the 535 games they were drawn, under version 1 in 164 of 498. It has not been set against its stock pilot. What it still casts in a share of games 15 points or more below stock AI's (the stock arm of ab-run #26, other tables of the same pool), 14 cards: Greater Tanuki, Ghoulish Impetus, The Mending of Dominaria, Heliod, God of the Sun, Battle for Bretagard, Starfield of Nyx and 8 more (demo-data/playtest/2026-11-14/pool-answers/enduring-enchantments-check.txt). VERSION 3 CANDIDATE `hooksopen` (2026-11-21). Version 2 with five changes: after Forge's own attack has been declared, the attackers sent at a player are sent at the opponent that looks most dangerous instead, when that opponent is ahead of the one attacked by five or more and the attack is no worse there: the damage sure to get through whatever is blocked is at least what it was, no more creatures there could block the attackers, and no attacker meets a blocker that would destroy it unless it met one where it was sent (`"aim": "danger"`; an attack that is sure to kill its target stays, and which creatures attack is not changed); and then the creatures that stayed home attack an opponent that has no creature that can block, the most dangerous such opponent first: those that deal damage, have no ability that taps them (or have vigilance) and are not wanted home by Forge's own judgement of the seat's defence (`"open": true`; a weaker opponent is not killed this way while a more dangerous one lives); and then a sure kill is taken from the most dangerous opponent down (`"finish": "leader"`: enough attackers are put on the opponent that looks most dangerous that the damage reaches its life whatever it blocks, then on the next one, and no weaker opponent is killed while a more dangerous one lives); and then a triggered ability of the seat that removes one permanent of an opponent (destroys it, exiles it, returns it to hand or library) is aimed at the opponent that looks most dangerous, when that opponent looks more dangerous than the one Forge aimed at by five or more and has a permanent of the same kind worth at least as much as Forge's choice or at least 4 (`"targets": {"triggers": "danger"}`); and then when Forge's blocks leave at least the seat's life in damage unblocked and blocks exist that would not, blocks are added, the least valuable free creatures in front of the heaviest unblocked attackers and only as many as it takes for the seat to live (`"block": {"survive": true}`). No cast or trigger rule is changed. SHIPPED 2026-11-22 as version 3: the `hooksopen` arm of ab-run #59 (seed 20261400, the tables of ab-run #58; demo-data/ab/2026-11-22-ab-v27/, DESIGN.md section 38). Beside version 2 on the same 200 tables of the pool: 75 wins against 69 (24 tables against 18, exact test 0.44); the `hooks` arm 69. Free damage is in because the arm with it won more of these tables than the arm without: the better of two on the tables that measured it; its confirming run on tables that chose nothing is still to be played (after ab-run #62, the exam of the five pool decks that got no hook). VERSION 4 CANDIDATE `guard`. Version 3 with one change: after Forge's own attack has been declared and the hooks the version already has have acted, attackers are taken back when the attack leaves the seat where the opponents one after another are sure to kill it before its next turn and keeping them home prevents that, or, when nothing kept home does, where one opponent alone is (`"guard": "table"`; a sure kill's attackers stay, and an attack stands when nothing kept home would save the seat). No cast or trigger rule is changed. SHIPPED 2026-11-22 as version 4: the `guard` arm of ab-run #63 (seed 20261450, tables that chose nothing; demo-data/ab/2026-11-22-ab-v31/, DESIGN.md section 40). On the same 200 tables of the pool: versions 2, 3 and 4 won 75, 73 and 72; version 3 beside 2 27 tables against 29 (exact test 0.89), version 4 beside 3 3 against 4 (exact test 1.00); dead with its own creatures tapped 12, 10 and 8 times. Read over the seven decks together by the rules fixed before the run: the versions with the hooks stand (139 tables against 142) and the guard holds (27 against 29; out before its next turn on 18 of the 175 tables its attack changed first, from 31).
